investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 allocatable VM slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~141–154 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is a Kubernetes infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on the peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peerpods nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, which is expected behavior for kata peerpods workloads, but if the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of peerpods-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient for the concurrent demand from the eval probes plus any live workloads, suggesting the node pool needs scaling.

QUATERNARY — Transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from evals or other workloads) temporarily exhausted the VM slots, which may self-resolve once existing agents are cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883).

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No preemption victims were available, so the pods timed out after ~141–154 seconds without ever starting, and the eval runner received no evidence payloads at all.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two eligible nodes (0/2 had capacity), and the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or selector rules. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) never completed, the agent lifecycle never progressed, and the eval returned zero evidence — causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) to be missing and the check to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity (0 allocatable VM slots), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~141–154 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is a Kubernetes infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on the peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. Preemption was also ruled out ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-peerpods nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, which is expected behavior for kata peerpods workloads, but if the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total number of peerpods-capable nodes (2) may be insufficient for the concurrent demand from the eval probes plus any live workloads, suggesting the node pool needs scaling.

QUATERNARY — Transient resource spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent creation requests (from evals or other workloads) temporarily exhausted the VM slots, which may self-resolve once existing agents are cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-18 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected assertion (message contains "hello from aura") unverifiable. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable until capacity is freed or expanded. This prevents agent creation from completing, which in turn prevents the eval runner from collecting any evidence, causing all three remote-agents checks to fail with identical scheduling error messages (evidence ids: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the call that submits the pod — this is the earliest failure boundary

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false, confirming the severity classification is correct
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity remains for new peer-pod VMs, blocking all remote agent creation attempts.

Secondary: The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, so the other 4 nodes cannot absorb overflow even if they have general compute headroom.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or concurrent workload may have left orphaned or long-running peer-pod VMs that are holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up, preventing new allocations.

Lower probability: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or node-level capacity configuration may have been reduced (e.g., by a node pool resize or config change), shrinking available slots below the demand level.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes immediately to determine current slot utilization and identify any orphaned or stuck peer-pod VMs consuming capacity.
If orphaned VMs are found, terminate them to free kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and allow new agent pods to schedule; then re-run the eval suite to confirm recovery.
If slots are legitimately exhausted by active workloads, evaluate expanding kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity by adding nodes with the required label or increasing the per-node vm slot limit.
Review whether the eval runner's withCleanup mechanism (run-status-probes.mjs) is reliably terminating remote agent pods after each eval run, to prevent slot leakage across runs.

Confirm the node affinity/selector on remote-agent pods is intentional and that the 4 non-kata nodes are correctly excluded; if the affinity is overly restrictive, consider whether additional nodes should be labeled.

Monitor the remote-agents feature health status given that remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are both required=true and degradedAfterFailures=1 — the feature is likely in a degraded or outage state per the registry configuration at infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187-188.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) vm slots, the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different scheduling or admission-controller issue should be investigated.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than sustained exhaustion.

If the Unschedulable message changes on re-run to a different error (e.g., image pull failure, admission webhook rejection, or quota exceeded at the namespace level), the root cause would be different from kata.peerpods.io/vm slot exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec was recently changed to exclude the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes (rather than those nodes being full), the cause would be a misconfigured affinity rule rather than capacity exhaustion.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass on a subsequent run, the shared scheduling layer would not be the cause and the failure would be localized to the runtime eval path specifically.

Add a scheduling-latency eval that measures pod-to-running time for remote agents and warns before the full Unschedulable timeout is reached, enabling earlier detection of capacity pressure.
Consider a dedicated eval for node affinity/selector correctness that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's scheduling constraints and carry available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity.
